title: launch-token-v2: SEP-41 with the narrowed transfer lock, holder rewards in two assets and hardened pool exclusion
brief:
Implement §6 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md.
- Base: OZ stellar-tokens 0.7.2 Base plus burnable, with overrides on transfer, transfer_from, burn and burn_from following the votes extension (oz fungible/extensions/votes/storage.rs:55-190).
- Transfer lock (§6.1, decision L4): before unlock a transfer succeeds only when from == launchpad, from ∈ lock_from (this launch's venue and fallback executors, constructor args, at most 2) or to == launchpad. Burns are always allowed. The locker is NOT exempt. unlock: launchpad only, once (at graduation or at rescue, L6).
- The token's own address holds the launch-token rewards: transfer, transfer_from, burn, burn_from and approve from `this` fail TokenAccount at any time, before and after unlock; transfers to `this` are allowed (§6.1, finding F1).
- Holder rewards (§6.2) when sharing_quote is Some, in two reward pools (decisions O1 and L13, finding F1): Q, the quote (curve fees and the quote side of harvests), and T, the launch token itself (the holders' half of the harvested token side, funded only by the locker after graduation and held at the token's own address). Per pool: reward-per-share with P = 1e18 and U256 intermediates, RewardPool {acc, queued, funded, paid, protocol_owed}; eligible and queued_ledger are shared. MIN_ELIGIBLE = 1 token; release only on a later ledger; self-transfers return early; an account is excluded when it is in FixedExcluded (instance, at most 5, includes the token itself) or its Holder entry says so (persistent, no cap); Holder entries {q_debt, q_owed, t_debt, t_owed, excluded} are written lazily; debts are rounded UP (mul_div_up_u256); Sharing is its own persistent entry. claim and sweep_protocol pay T through the internal update with the hook (the receiver is settled at its old balance first; claim zeroes t_owed before paying).
- exclude(account): launchpad only. exclude_pool(kind, other, pool): anyone, with the checks of §6.2 (decision L5, finding F2): pool.executable() is a Wasm contract and pool ∉ {this, other} (NotAPool); Soroswap: factory.get_pair(this, other) == pool and the pair's token_0/token_1 are {this, other}; Aquarius: gated only by AQUARIUS_POOL_LOOKUP_OK (CT-03's check 4), never by the overall Aquarius venue go/no-go, then the router's pool lookup for sorted(this, other) contains pool, the pool's token list equals sorted(this, other) and share_id() is a Wasm contract outside {pool, this, other}; the floor: bal(pool) ≥ EXCLUDE_MIN_BALANCE (1e10, 1,000 tokens) or the pool's pending rewards ≥ EXCLUDE_MIN_OWED (1e6) in Q or ≥ EXCLUDE_MIN_BALANCE in T (BelowFloor). The Aquarius router is a required constructor argument (Address, not Option). Both functions are idempotent and move the account's settled owed in both pools into protocol_owed.
- The treasury (finding V2): a constructor argument (the launchpad's treasury at launch). With sharing on it is excluded at construction through its Holder flag. exclude_treasury() -> bool: anyone; with sharing off it returns false; otherwise exclude_account(launchpad.treasury(), false), idempotent and one-way (a former treasury stays excluded). sweep_protocol excludes the current treasury before paying it. The locker calls exclude_treasury before it pays this token's base side; the launchpad never calls it (re-entry). FixedExcluded (the launchpad, the locker, the two executors and the token itself) is unchanged. Invariant I-T10.
- notify_reward(notifier, asset, amount): launchpad or locker only; asset is the quote or the token itself (UnsupportedAsset otherwise); amount > 0; funding check per asset (quote: quote.balance(this) ≥ funded − paid + amount; T: the token's own balance ≥ funded − paid + amount). claim(holder) -> (quote, token) (excluded accounts refused), sweep_protocol() -> (quote, token) paying launchpad.treasury(), and the views of §6.4 (pending_rewards and queued_rewards per asset, exclusion_floor).
- Errors (15, numbered ERR_BASE + 2·100 + n, finding V10) and events (each reward event carries its asset) exactly as §6.4. No admin, and no instance TTL extension in user calls.
acceptance: Every row of the §6.1 path table holds before unlock: holder→holder, holder→executor, holder→pool and holder→locker are refused; launchpad→holder, holder→launchpad, launchpad→executor, executor→pool and executor→launchpad are allowed; burns are allowed. unlock works once, from the launchpad only.
transfer, transfer_from, burn, burn_from and approve from the token's own address fail TokenAccount before and after unlock; only claim and sweep_protocol lower that balance (I-T8)
With sharing off, behaviour equals the v1 launch-token, and the 6 v1 tests are ported and pass

Property test (proptest, 1,000 cases in CI) over random transfers, self-transfers, burns, burn_from, exclude and exclude_pool, notifies of both assets, ledger advances and claims against a Rust reference model: I-T1 to I-T10 hold per asset, no claim or sweep ever fails for lack of funds (I-T2 with debts rounded up), and each holder's claim in each asset equals the model to within 1 unit per release
A flash test (receive tokens, notify, claim and send away in one ledger) earns 0 in both assets; a claim of launch-token rewards earns nothing on the claimed amount

exclude_pool accepts the real Soroswap fixture pair of (token, other) above the floor; rejects an account address, a fake contract, a pair of another token and a pair whose token list doesn't match (NotAPool) and a pool below the floor (BelowFloor); is idempotent; moves the pool's stranded owed in both pools to protocol_owed; sweep_protocol pays both to launchpad.treasury()
The Aquarius branch of exclude_pool works against CT-03's fixtures whenever AQUARIUS_POOL_LOOKUP_OK is true, also with AQUARIUS_VENUE_OK false, and returns UnsupportedVenue only when check 4 failed
Below MIN_ELIGIBLE, rewards of either asset go to protocol_owed
notify_reward without funds fails UnderFunded, with 0 fails ZeroAmount, with another asset fails UnsupportedAsset, and from anyone but the launchpad or locker fails NotNotifier

The treasury is excluded at construction; after the test launchpad's treasury changes, exclude_treasury excludes the new one (idempotent, true once) and the old one stays excluded; sweep_protocol and a locker-funded payout never pay launch tokens to an eligible treasury, and the treasury's pending rewards stay 0; with sharing off exclude_treasury returns false (I-T10, finding V2)
Release WASM ≤ 64 KB; cost_estimate for a sharing transfer stays ≤ 30M instructions and ≤ 6 write entries

title: exec-aquarius, Aquarius client traits and WASM fixtures (five-check go/no-go gate)
brief:
Implement §7 (rules) and §7.2 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md, and run the five-check go/no-go gate (decision L2).
- Fetch the Aquarius testnet router CBCFTQSPDBAIZ6R6PJQKSQWKNKWH2QIV3I4J72SHWBIK3ADRRAM5A6GD, a standard pool and the share token WASMs with tools/fetch-fixtures.sh (read-only RPC, no keys). Record them in fixtures.json with notes.
- Fill contracts/common/src/aquarius.rs with #[contractclient] traits for exactly the router and pool functions the fixtures confirm: the pool-creation payment getter, init_standard_pool, deposit, the pool lookup for a token pair, the pool's token-list getter and share_id (used by launch-token-v2's exclude_pool), withdraw by share amount (used by lp-locker's harvest) and total shares. Record the router's pool-creation event name in fixtures.json for CT-15.
- Record each gate check's result separately and set the two compile-time flags in common/src/aquarius.rs: AQUARIUS_POOL_LOOKUP_OK (check 4 with the token-list getter and share_id) and AQUARIUS_VENUE_OK (all five). launch-token-v2's exclusion of Aquarius pools depends only on the first, because anyone can open an Aquarius pool for an unlocked token (decision L5, finding F2); the venue and the locker's Aquarius harvest depend on the second.
- exec-aquarius: __constructor(router, payment_asset, max_pool_payment, callers). graduate applies the caller rule (L4); finds the standard pool for fee_fraction ∈ {10, 30, 100} (testnet uses 30); creates a missing pool from the AQUA float only when the router's payment asset equals payment_asset, amount ≤ max_pool_payment (PaymentTooHigh) and float ≥ amount (PaymentUnavailable), with an exact authorize_as_current_contract entry; requires total shares == 0 (PoolNotEmpty); calls router.deposit with every deeper transfer pre-authorized; sends the share token to lp_to; returns leftovers to source. Views float, pool_payment and max_pool_payment.
- The gate (§7.2): (1) the payment getter and the auth trees of init_standard_pool and deposit; (2) during deposit the launch token moves only executor → pool (prove it with a test-only token that refuses every other path, mimicking launch-token-v2's lock); (3) the reserve-holding address equals the returned pool; (4) the pool lookup, the pool's token list and share_id; (5) withdraw by shares. If any check fails, stop and write a no-go naming the failing check; Aquarius then stays disabled as a venue in the deploy economics, and common/src/aquarius.rs keeps only what was confirmed, with AQUARIUS_POOL_LOOKUP_OK still true when check 4 passed.
- exec-aquarius numbers its errors with err_code, tag 4 (PaymentUnavailable = 10_404, PaymentTooHigh = 10_405, finding V10). Record the Aquarius fixtures' error codes from their contract specs and confirm none falls in 10_100–11_099.
- For CT-11's float-funding swap (finding V8), record in fixtures.json notes the router's swap and estimate functions, the testnet XLM–AQUA standard pool and the testnet AQUA asset (code, issuer, SAC id).
- Views float, pool_payment and max_pool_payment let the deploy script and the keeper compare the float with its target (50 × the pool payment on the owner's testnet, 10 × on testnet-qa) and alert below 5 × (finding F11).
acceptance: Fixture sha256s and source contract ids are recorded; no key material
Graduation into a new pool works and pays exactly the router's configured amount from the float; an amount above max_pool_payment fails PaymentTooHigh
An existing empty pool is reused without payment; a pool that already has shares fails PoolNotEmpty
A caller outside callers fails NotCaller and the float is unchanged (the drain probe of review B2)
A short float returns a recoverable error through try_, and the harness's balances roll back
Share tokens arrive at lp_to; leftovers return to source; the reserves sit at the returned pool address
With the lock-mimicking test token, deposit succeeds and no pool → executor transfer of that token is attempted
Withdraw by shares, the pool lookup, the pool's token list and share_id work against the fixtures
Or: a written no-go naming the failing check, in which case Aquarius stays disabled as a venue in deploy economics; the two flags in common/src/aquarius.rs record which checks passed

fixtures.json records the router's swap and estimate functions, the testnet XLM–AQUA pool and the AQUA asset and SAC for CT-11 (finding V8); exec-aquarius errors are 10_401–10_407, and no Aquarius fixture error code falls in 10_100–11_099 (finding V10)

title: lp-locker: permanent LP custody, fee-growth harvest without a price guard, both-sides payouts
brief:
Implement §8 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md.
- The constructor fixes the owners (launchpad-v2 and moments-v2, by precomputed ids), the Soroswap factory, the Aquarius router (Option) and harvest_interval, validated with dyor-common's bounds (60 s to 1 day; 3600 in production, 60 on testnet-qa) and readable through harvest_interval(). launchpad-v2 and moments-v2 require it to equal their durations.harvest_interval (finding F6).
- register: owners only; 1 ≤ harvest_bps ≤ BPS (InvalidHarvestBps); checks LP received against Tracked; records the principal in √k units (U256); last_harvest = now.
- No poke and no price guard (decision L12). harvest guards: the kind is harvestable (Soroswap; Aquarius only when AQUARIUS_VENUE_OK), and now ≥ last_harvest + harvest_interval.
- harvest maths: growth = current − principal; take = min(growth·harvest_bps/BPS, current·MAX_HARVEST_ROUND_BPS/BPS); withdraw ΔL (Soroswap: transfer LP to the pair, then withdraw; Aquarius: withdraw by shares); principal = min(principal + mul_div_up(take, BPS − harvest_bps, harvest_bps), current − take). The compounded part is proportional to what was taken, so compounded : harvested = (BPS − hb) : hb in every round, also when the 0.5% cap binds (finding F7); at MOMENT_HARVEST_BPS 6667 that is 3,333 : 6,667, not exactly 1 : 2 (finding V3).
- Payouts from owner.harvest_payees(reference) → HarvestPayees {quote, base}: when the base list has a notify payee (a sharing launch's token), first call its exclude_treasury(), so the current treasury is excluded before it receives launch tokens (finding V2); each side is split by its own payee list (the last payee gets the remainder), zero amounts skipped; notify payees get asset.transfer(this, token, x) then token.notify_reward(this, asset, x), which for a launch's base side funds launch-token rewards; other payees get try_transfer with an Owed fallback; an empty list burns that side (Moments' coin side). Launches send the same 50/50 list on both sides (decisions O1 and L13, finding F1).
- withdraw_owed and the views (harvestable includes next_at; harvest_interval). The harvested event carries take and compounded.
- No principal withdrawal path, no admin and no setters. Errors are numbered ERR_BASE + 6·100 + n (finding V10).
acceptance: After random swaps on a Soroswap fixture, the locked position's √k value never falls below its principal (I-K1). Property test, 1,000 cases.
TooSoon before the interval; NothingToHarvest without growth; UnsupportedKind for HoldOnly and QaFail, and for Aquarius when AQUARIUS_VENUE_OK is false
The cap holds: no round withdraws more than 0.5% of the position's LP, and capped growth stays harvestable in later rounds

harvest_bps 10000 keeps the principal constant; at 6667, compounded : harvested equals (BPS − hb) : hb = 3,333 : 6,667 within rounding in every round (not 1 : 2, finding V3), with the cap binding and not binding (property test, finding F7); harvest_bps 0 or above BPS is refused at register

Both sides follow the payee lists: the launch case pays 50% to the treasury and 50% to the recipient (sharing off) or to the token with notify_reward for the right asset (sharing on) on each side; the Moments case pays the quote side 40/60 and burns the base side; a payee without a trustline gets Owed on either side and withdraw_owed pays later; zero payouts are skipped; with a notify payee on the base side, exclude_treasury is called on that token before any base-side payout (finding V2)
The §8.3 bound: moving the price 4x before a harvest does not lower the withdrawn value at the true price, and the base/quote mix shift stays within one round's quote side
harvest_interval() returns the constructor value; values below 60 s or above 1 day are refused
Every non-view entry point other than register is permissionless, and no function moves principal LP to any address
Release WASM ≤ 64 KB

title: launchpad-v2: curve, 10 XLM booked launch fee, SAC-only quotes, terms, venues, guarded graduation with a fallback delay, pro-rata rescue, creator recipient, recoverable guardian
brief:
Implement §5 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md completely.
- Curve maths: v1 curve.rs with Monad's clamp (net = min(net, remaining); the snipe bucket absorbs rounding; M:contracts/src/BondingCurve.sol:258-274).
- Constructor: durations validated with dyor-common (with fallback_delay and harvest_interval); requires locker.harvest_interval() == durations.harvest_interval (InvalidConfig, finding F6); checks that the XLM address is a Stellar Asset Contract; the initial venue table in order (ids follow it).
- launch: salt from creator + nonce with NonceUsed and the token_address view (decision L15); the 10 XLM fee (decision O6) moves creator → launchpad and is booked as curve.launch_fee_due; expected LaunchTerms by value, durations included; the token is deployed with lock_from, fixed_excluded, sharing_quote, the Soroswap factory, the Aquarius router (always passed, finding F2) and the current treasury, which the token excludes from holder rewards (finding V2); temporary Exempt entry; initial buy. launch writes no instance key.
- set_quote accepts only a Stellar Asset Contract (asset.executable() == Some(Executable::StellarAsset), else QuoteNotSac, finding F17).
- Trading: every fee, split and snipe value comes from the launch's own pinned Launch record (fee_bps, protocol_share_bps, creator_fee_bps, snipe_schedule, snipe_step_secs), never from Config, as Monad pins per curve and per pool (M:contracts/src/BondingCurve.sol:294; LaunchpadFactory.sol:539; MemeHook.sol:233-234; finding V1). Snipe by ledger timestamp in snipe_step_secs (5 s, L11); fee routing to curve.protocol_fees, curve.creator_fees or the holders (transfer to the token, then notify_reward(this, quote, x)); completion at real_quote == threshold, with no graduation attempt (L3).
- graduate (the launch's venue only) and graduate_fallback (the fallback venue only, and only from stuck_since + fallback_delay, else FallbackTooEarly, finding F14) through try_ into the executor with exact pre-auth; a failure is decoded with dyor-common's grad_failure and recorded as grad_fail{venue, origin, code, …} and Failed(GradFailure) (finding V10). The result checks of §5.5 panic GraduationInvalid. After success: exclude the pool, unlock, burn the whole remaining balance (L7), dust to protocol_fees, locker.register with LAUNCH_HARVEST_BPS = 10000, stuck_since reset.
- Stuck: stuck_since on the first recoverable failure; mark_stuck after the grace; the venue-locked fallback rule (locked_fallback delay or allow_fallback) on top of fallback_delay.
- rescue: admin from rescue_admin, anyone from rescue_public (O2); burn the launchpad's balance, unlock (L6), snapshot refund_quote and refund_supply. refund: pro-rata, no fees, burns the holder's tokens.
- Creator recipient: transfer; takeover in temporary storage (wait + window; cancel by the admin or the recipient); on any change the booked creator fees move to CreatorOwed(old, quote) (L14); claim_owed. Unharvested LP growth is the declared exception (finding F3).
- Treasury and venue proposals with the timelock and window; cancel by the admin or the guardian (L8). Guardian (finding F16): two-step handoff (transfer_guardian, accept_guardian), renounce_guardian; the admin's propose_guardian / apply_guardian / cancel_guardian through the timelock, which the guardian can't cancel and a handoff doesn't clear.
- claim_protocol_fees(tokens ≤ 20) to the treasury current at the call (lead default, finding F3), whitelist, launch pause, status (with fallback_at) and every view.
- harvest_payees returns the same list for the quote and the base side, built from the launch's pinned Launch.protocol_share_bps, never Config (finding V1): [treasury ps, then the token (notify) when sharing is on or the recipient when it is off, BPS − ps] (decisions O1 and L13, finding F1). The treasury holds the launch tokens it receives; nothing sells them (lead default, finding V2).
- Errors (37, numbered ERR_BASE + 1·100 + n, finding V10) and events exactly as §5.6–5.7. No upgrade function and no instance TTL extension in user calls.
acceptance: All 14 v1 launchpad tests and 4 curve tests are ported; buy_clamps_at_threshold asserts net == remaining exactly

Terms mismatch on any single field (durations included) fails TermsChanged; a reused nonce fails NonceUsed; two creators' launches built against the same pre-state both apply, and launch writes no instance key

The 10 XLM fee (100,000,000 stroops) moves only creator → launchpad and is booked on the launch; claim_protocol_fees sends it and the quote-side protocol fees to the treasury current at the call in one transfer per asset; more than 20 tokens fail TooManyTokens; a treasury without the quote's trustline makes the whole call fail with nothing moved
set_quote with a Wasm token or an account address fails QuoteNotSac; a SAC is accepted (I-L11); a constructor with a locker whose harvest_interval differs from the durations fails InvalidConfig
The snipe tax steps at 0/5/10/15/20 s; exempt buyers, the creator and the initial recipient pay none; more than 32 exemptions fail

With sharing on, the creator part reaches the token and holders can claim it in the next ledger; with sharing off, claim_creator_fees pays the current recipient; after a recipient change the earlier fees are claimable only by the old recipient through claim_owed

harvest_payees returns the same 50/50 list for both sides, with the token as the notify payee when sharing is on and the recipient when it is off; after a treasury change it names the new treasury; set_fees with a different protocol_share_bps after graduation leaves harvest_payees and the next harvest's split unchanged, and during the curve leaves that launch's route_fees split unchanged (finding V1)
Completion closes buys and sells; graduate on Soroswap succeeds at the curve's final price (I-L6); the pool is excluded before any later-ledger release; the LP is registered; stuck_since is 0 (I-L9)

A recoverable executor failure leaves reserves, balances and lock state unchanged (I-L5), sets stuck_since once, and retries don't move it; graduate_fallback fails FallbackTooEarly until stuck_since + fallback_delay, also right after a single transient failure (I-L12), and a primary retry inside the delay graduates on the creator's venue; graduate_fallback never calls the primary executor (a test executor panics if called again); a recoverable failure is recorded with the executor's namespaced origin and code (exec-soroswap PoolNotEmpty as origin 3, code 10_303; qa-exec-fail ForcedFailure as origin 5, code 10_502, finding V10)
Test executors that over-report or under-report the used amounts, report a wrong pool, or send the LP elsewhere make graduate abort with GraduationInvalid and change nothing

Rescue is refused before rescue_admin, admin-only until rescue_public, open to anyone after; the token unlocks; refunds pay floor(tokens·refund_quote/refund_supply) in any order (property test), Σ refunds ≤ refund_quote, and buys and sells stay closed

The guardian can cancel treasury and venue proposals and nothing else; the handoff needs accept_guardian; the admin's guardian replacement applies after the timelock, the guardian can't cancel it and a handoff doesn't clear it; every privileged function rejects a wrong signer (mock_auths); admin calls never change a live launch (I-L4)

With sharing on, the launch token is built with the treasury excluded; after apply_treasury, the next harvest excludes the new treasury before paying it launch tokens, and the treasury's pending rewards stay 0 in both assets (finding V2)
Release WASM ≤ 110 KB

title: moment-nft: one SEP-50 contract per Moment, edition number = token id
brief:
Implement §10 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md (decision L9).
- Constructor (minter, name, symbol, metadata_uri, creator, royalty_bps, media_hash, place, date, external_url). The contract's address is the Moment's id; there is no numeric moment id.
- Built on OZ NonFungibleToken Base with the royalties default set to the creator.
- mint(to, qty): minter only, 1 to 20, sequential edition numbers from 1 via Base::mint, refused once closed.
- close(): minter only, once; freezes edition_size; emits closed.
- token_uri returns the Moment's metadata URI. Provenance views: media_hash, place, date, external_url.
- No burn and no admin. Errors are numbered ERR_BASE + 8·100 + n (finding V10).
acceptance: Edition numbers start at 1 and are contiguous across mints; the first edition number is returned
Minting after close and closing twice both fail; edition_size equals minted
royalty_info pays royalty_bps to the creator
Only the minter can mint or close (auth test)
cost_estimate for mint(…, 20) is ≤ 25 write entries

title: moment-coin: capped, burnable per-Moment SEP-41 coin
brief:

title: moments-graduator: atomic coin deployment and Soroswap seeding
acceptance: coin_address(nft) equals the deployed coin address
On success the pool opens at reserve/pool_coins, the LP is at the locker, and coin total_supply equals pool_coins minus any burned leftover
A forced failure through try_ leaves no coin contract deployed, and the moments harness keeps its USDC

A lying executor (qa-exec-fail mode 2, or a test executor reporting a wrong pool or wrong amounts) makes graduate return GraduationInvalid through try_, with no coin deployed and every balance unchanged
Only the configured moments address can call graduate; exec-soroswap refuses a graduator that is not in its callers

A test executor that seeds the pool with fewer coins than pool_coins while reporting the full amount, or reports token_used outside [pool_coins − 1 bp, pool_coins], or liquidity below the minimum, is rejected through try_ with GraduationInvalid (11_003), with no coin deployed and every balance unchanged (finding V9)

title: moments-v2: policy, NFT-addressed publish, collect, keeper graduation, vesting, expiry
brief:
Implement §9 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md.
- Governance and guardian, with the dual pause. Policy propose/apply/cancel with the timelock and window from the durations, and Monad's validation adapted to 7 dp.
- publish with expected MomentsTerms by value (durations and harvest constants included), USDC only (L9), the price ceiling, an NFT deployed per Moment with salt from creator + nonce (L15, NonceUsed), the predicted coin address from graduator.coin_address(nft), and the bundle rate. Moments are keyed by NFT address; there is no MomentCount, and publish and collect write no instance key.

title: v2 deploy and owner admin scripts, testnet and testnet-qa economics, QA profile guards, reviewed-hash check
brief:
§14, §16 and §17 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md.
deploy-contracts-v2.ts --deployment <testnet|testnet-qa> [--dry-run] [--aquarius auto|off] [--fund-aqua-float]:
- checks every v2 WASM's sha256 against contracts/review/reviewed-wasm.sha256 (written by CT-19) with lib/reviewed-hashes.ts and refuses a missing file or any mismatch, for testnet and testnet-qa alike; a dry run prints the comparison (decision L16, finding F13);
- uploads the v2 WASMs; precomputes every singleton id from (deployer, fixed salt) with contract-ids.ts;
- deploys in order: the executors (callers = launchpad-v2 and moments-graduator), the locker (harvest_interval from the durations), the graduator, launchpad-v2 (initial venue table, durations, TTL policy, guardian) and moments-v2 (durations, policy, guardian), with peers as constructor args;
- configures quotes (Stellar Asset Contracts only), venues and policy from economics/<name>-v2.json; reads the venue table back from venues() and uses those ids everywhere (finding F8);
- writes _shared/deployments/<name>-v2.json (ids, the venue table with ids and kinds as read from the chain, aquarius {enabled, reason}, WASM hashes, public roles, durations, deploy ledger, generation entry; never a key; no skip list).
Any other deployment name, mainnet included, is refused (decision O4).
v2-profile.ts holds the production and testnet-qa duration sets (equal to dyor-common's, with fallback_delay, harvest_interval and pending_backstop, findings F6 and V11) and the guards: QA durations, qa-exec-fail, the failing Moments stack, key generation and SMOKE=1 are refused for every deployment except testnet-qa (O3).
Keys:
- testnet (the owner's deploy, O5): DEPLOYER_SECRET read silently from the environment; ADMIN_PUBLIC, LAUNCHPAD_GUARDIAN_PUBLIC, GOVERNANCE_PUBLIC, MOMENTS_GUARDIAN_PUBLIC and TREASURY_PUBLIC as public addresses; the launchpad guardian must differ from the admin and the Moments guardian from governance;
- testnet-qa: throwaway QA keys (deployer, admin, guardians, governance, treasury, QA asset issuer, qa-exec-fail admin) generated into a git-ignored file under .secrets/ (mode 600), written and read only by the scripts; never print a secret.
Preflight: the treasury exists and trusts every enabled classic quote asset (USDC on testnet; USDC and the QA asset on testnet-qa), because claim_protocol_fees is all-or-nothing per call (finding F9). On testnet-qa the script creates the QA treasury's USDC and QA-asset trustlines before the preflight.
testnet-qa extras: the QA test asset and its SAC; one qa-exec-fail instance (callers = launchpad-v2 and the failing stack's graduator; qa_admin = the QA key) as one venue; the venue-locked QA quote with venues_allowed = [the qa-exec-fail id as read] and fallback = the Soroswap id as read; the failing Moments stack (a second moments-v2 and moments-graduator from the same WASMs, with qa-exec-fail as the graduator's executor, finding F5). The keeper skip list is CT-15's lite.keeper_skip table, not part of the deployment file.
Aquarius float (findings F11 and V8): if CT-03 was a go and --aquarius isn't off, the script acquires the AQUA before it deploys anything, because the venue table is a launchpad constructor argument. It adds an AQUA trustline to the deployer and swaps XLM → AQUA through the Aquarius testnet router's XLM–AQUA pool (functions, pool and asset from CT-03's fixtures.json notes), after a depth check: estimate 1 XLM and the full amount, and require the full amount to return at least the target (10 × pool_payment on testnet-qa, 50 × on testnet) plus 10% at an average rate within 3% of the 1-XLM rate, spending at most 2,000 XLM. After deploying exec-aquarius it sends the AQUA through the AQUA SAC and reports float() against the target. On testnet-qa the step runs by default from the QA deployer; if the depth check or the swap fails, or with --aquarius off, the script deploys without exec-aquarius and without the Aquarius venue and writes aquarius {enabled: false, reason} into the deployment file. On the owner's testnet the swap runs only with --fund-aqua-float (from the owner's deployer key); otherwise the script reports the float for the owner to fund.
Economics files (§14.1–14.2): launch fee 10 XLM (decision O6); XLM phantom 2,000; USDC phantom 20 (L10); Aquarius as venue with fee_fraction 30 and max_pool_payment 10 AQUA only if CT-03 was a go (L2); Moments threshold 10 USDC and the policy of §14.2.
admin-v2.ts builds unsigned XDR for: rescue, allow_fallback, takeover propose and cancel, treasury propose and cancel (admin or guardian), venue propose, cancel and enable, quotes, the guardian handoff (transfer, accept, renounce) and the admin's guardian replacement (propose, apply, cancel), policy propose/apply/cancel, pauses, and the v1 cutover (v1 launchpad set_launches_enabled(false); v1 Moments set_policy with the current platform and royalty values read from config() and publishing false). It reads the signing account's signers and thresholds and refuses to build when one signer can meet a multi-signer account's medium threshold alone. It never signs and never submits.
Nothing runs against a live network in this package.

title: Internal three-reviewer security review: the gate before every deployment, testnet-qa included
files: contracts/review/reviewed-wasm.sha256 (written at exit: the reviewed lines of contracts/dist/SHA256SUMS and the commit they were built from; hashes only, never finding text)
brief:
§19.1 of DESIGN-stellar-contracts-v2.revised.md. Decision L16: no deployment of any kind (testnet-qa or the owner's testnet) happens before this review exits. The review covers the contracts, the scripts, the backend and CT-18's API wiring and e2e script (finding F13).
Three independent reviewers:
- R1, economics and maths: curve and Monad clamp; pro-rata refund rounding; reward-per-share rounding (debts rounded up) and overflow in both reward assets; harvest maths, the both-sides 50/50 split by the launch's pinned share (V1), the compounding ratio (3,333 : 6,667, V3) when the cap binds and the sandwich bound of §8.3; the F3 backlog bound (V7); the treasury's exclusion from holder rewards (V2); Moments harvest constants and the burn's pool-depth effect (V4); vesting; supply identity; the exclusion floor; differential vectors;
